Export template doesn't include arm64 simulator binaries at all. It's impossible to build with OSXCross. There was code to generate simulatore binaries from device binary, but it was removed some time ago.

Simulator build is almost useless in any case, since it does not support Metal in required capacity. On ARM mqcs you can simply run iOS apps directly.

We probably should remove x86-64 simulator build and all mentions of simulation from the official template. There's very little practical use for it, it's just wasting space and creating unreasonable expectations.
OP mentions that it worked in 4.6.1. Was that a mistake?

Yes, apologies, I meant to say this doesn't work, even on 4.6.1
I would suggest removing the simulator stuff completely and making a note of WHY it doesn't work.

Not to go counter-current but..
I just managed to make it all work!! 

Well me.. or Claude AI who's an absolute **Beast** when it comes to Xcode commands..

-In Godot 4.6.2 Stable
First I managed to create Custom Templates by generating the proper intermediate files, 
and inserting them on the Stock templates, changing the internal config, and creating a custom ios.zip file.

(that required a couple days of grinding and will require a manual on its own..)

This is important because the Stock template doesn't have all the necessary iOS Simulator files or config inside.
So the first step is creating proper OS Templates with correct Simulator support.

-Then what we accomplished is considerable..

My app has:
Custom GDExt C++ Library (complex Audio DSP and Graphs)
Custom GDExt Plugins - Audio Capture, and Attest
Asset Store Plugins - Admob, In-App Purchases

It's a 2D Audio App, and thus it's meant to use OpenGL only, 
no Vulkan or 3D or any kind, altho it also incorporates 2 Shaders.

In iOS/MacOS the base foundation of Metal API needs to be included on your Template and build tho,
or it will not work sans-Metal with only OpenGL..

-Believe it or not, 
with what we just did, all of it works 100% Perfectly!

Audio Capture Plugin - App is able to Capture Audio, and Process it.
GDext Library working perfectly..

Admob Plugin - Working Perfectly and showing Banners and GDPR Consent via UMP
IAP Purchase and Storekit - Working Perfectly, fetching real Price from Apple and allowing Purchase/restore.

Attest - Working perfectly, but not doing anything cause Attest is not meant to run in Simulator environment..

-Now this is the simplified version with placeholder names,
let's see if I can lay it clear enough..

*The Poing Admob Plugin, and In-App Purchases Plugin work perfectly by default,
no need to fix anything for them..

Prerequisites:,
having a working App and Build, 
and Custom Template with iOS Simulator support.

The core issue is that Godot exports device-only frameworks and incorrectly tagged simulator dylibs,
which the iOS Simulator cannot load.

```
================================================================================
  iOS SIMULATOR POST-EXPORT FIX COMMANDS
  Godot 4.6.2 Stable / Macbook M3 w/ Sequoia
================================================================================

This guide explains how to make Godot 4.6 iOS exports work on the iOS Simulator when using GDExtensions,
by fixing dylib platform tags and converting frameworks into xcframeworks.

Run all commands from the Export Root folder.

STEP 1 - Fix simulator dylib platform tag (IOS - IOSSIMULATOR)
================================================================================

The main Custom GDExtension lib simulator dylib is incorrectly tagged as platform IOS instead of IOSSIMULATOR. 
They must be tagged as IOSSIMULATOR or dyld will reject them.

Fix with vtool using numeric platform ID (7 = IOSSIMULATOR).
The plugin dylibs are already correctly tagged ? no vtool needed for them.

vtool -set-build-version 7 14.0 26.2 \
  -replace -output \
  "/Godot_ Project/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib" \
  "/Godot_Project/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib"

Verify:
vtool -show "/Godot_Project/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib"
Should show: platform IOSSIMULATOR

STEP 2 - Fix dylib install names (@rpath)
================================================================================

All three Custom Simulator dylibs have their install name set to a bare relative path
(e.g. bin/ios/YourLib...) which dyld on the simulator cannot resolve at runtime.
Fix with install_name_tool to use @rpath instead.

NOTE: This only needs to be done ONCE per build of the simulator dylibs.
      Once fixed in the source project, the fix persists across exports.
      Only redo if you rebuild the simulator dylibs from scratch.

install_name_tool -id "@rpath/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib" \
  "/Godot_Project/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib"

install_name_tool -id "@rpath/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib" \
  "/Godot_Project/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib"

install_name_tool -id "@rpath/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib" \
  "/Godot_Project/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib"

Verify all three:
otool -L "/Godot_Project/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib" | head -3
otool -L "/Godot_Project/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib" | head -3
otool -L "/Godot_Project/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib" | head -3

Each should show @rpath/YourLib... as the first entry.

STEP 3 ? Create xcframeworks from device + simulator dylibs
================================================================================

Godot's export wraps dylibs in plain .framework bundles (device only).
We replace them with proper .xcframework bundles containing both slices.

# Remove old plain frameworks and any previous xcframeworks from export
rm -rf "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.framework"
rm -rf "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.framework"
rm -rf "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.framework"
rm -rf "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework"
rm -rf "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework"
rm -rf "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB.xcframework"

GODOT_PROJECT="/Folders/Godot_Project"

# Create Plugin 1 xcframework
xcodebuild -create-xcframework \
  -library "$GODOT_PROJECT/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.dylib" \
  -library "$GODOT_PROJECT/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib" \
  -output "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework"

# Create Plugin 2 xcframework
xcodebuild -create-xcframework \
  -library "$GODOT_PROJECT/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.dylib" \
  -library "$GODOT_PROJECT/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.simulator.dylib" \
  -output "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework"

# Create main GDExtension Lib xcframework
xcodebuild -create-xcframework \
  -library "$GODOT_PROJECT/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.dylib" \
  -library "$GODOT_PROJECT/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.dylib" \
  -output "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB.xcframework"

STEP 4 - Patch the Xcode project file to reference xcframeworks
================================================================================

Godot may generate the pbxproj with quoted or unquoted strings depending on the
export. Run BOTH sed commands - one will match, the other will be a no-op.

# For unquoted pbxproj format:
sed -i '' \
  -e 's|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.framework; name = GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.framework; path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.ios.template_release.universal.framework|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework; name = GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework; path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework|g' \
  -e 's|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.framework; name = GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.framework; path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.ios.template_release.universal.framework|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework; name = GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework; path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework|g' \
  -e 's|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.framework; name = GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.framework; path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB.ios.template_release.arm64.framework|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework; name = GDEXT_LIB.xcframework; path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB.xcframework|g' \
  PROJECT_NAME.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj

# For quoted pbxproj format:
sed -i '' \
  -e 's|lastKnownFileType = wrapper\.framework; name = "GDEXT_PLUG1\.ios\.template_release\.universal\.framework"; path = "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1\.ios\.template_release\.universal\.framework"|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework; name = "GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework"; path = "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME1/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework"|g' \
  -e 's|lastKnownFileType = wrapper\.framework; name = "GDEXT_PLUG2\.ios\.template_release\.universal\.framework"; path = "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2\.ios\.template_release\.universal\.framework"|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework; name = "GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework"; path = "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/addons/PLUG_NAME2/bin/ios/GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework"|g' \
  -e 's|lastKnownFileType = wrapper\.framework; name = "GDEXT_LIB\.ios\.template_release\.arm64\.framework"; path = "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB\.ios\.template_release\.arm64\.framework"|lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework; name = "GDEXT_LIB.xcframework"; path = "EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/bin/GDEXT_LIB.xcframework"|g' \
  PROJECT_NAME.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj

Verify:
grep -n "lib name" PROJECT_NAME.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj
The PBXFileReference should show:
  lastKnownFileType = wrapper.xcframework
  name = GDEXT_PLUG1.xcframework / GDEXT_PLUG2.xcframework / GDEXT_LIB.xcframework
  path = EXPORT_ROOT/dylibs/.../lib_names_*.xcframework

STEP 5 ? Clear DerivedData and rebuild in Xcode
================================================================================

rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/PROJECT_NAME-XXX

Then open Xcode and apply the normal Config Settings for your build.

Select the desired Simulator device.

Press Build/Run; App should Install and Run on the Simulator..

Voila?

NOTES
================================================================================

- Steps 1 and 2 only need to be done ONCE per simulator dylib build.
  The fixes are applied to the source dylibs in the Godot project folder
  and persist across exports. Only redo if you rebuild the dylibs.

- Steps 3, 4, 5 must be repeated after every fresh Godot export.

================================================================================
END
```

Still present in **4.7.1.stable** — the report above covers 4.6.2, so confirming
the regression survived into 4.7.x.

**Environment**
- Godot `4.7.1.stable.steam.a13da4feb`, macOS on Apple Silicon (M4), Xcode 26 (iPhoneOS 26.5 SDK)
- Template: `export_templates/4.7.stable/ios.zip` (202,038,609 bytes, dated 2026-06-18)

**The xcframework still advertises arm64 while the archive is x86_64-only**, in both
the debug and release variants:

    $ plutil -p libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework/Info.plist
      "LibraryIdentifier" => "ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"
      "SupportedArchitectures" => [ "arm64", "x86_64" ]
      "SupportedPlatformVariant" => "simulator"

    $ lipo -info libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libgodot.a
    Non-fat file: ... is architecture: x86_64

    $ lipo -info libgodot.ios.release.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libgodot.a
    Non-fat file: ... is architecture: x86_64

**Impact:** an exported Xcode project cannot be built for the iOS Simulator on Apple
Silicon. Xcode picks the slice from the Info.plist (which claims arm64), then fails at
link time. Rosetta/x86_64 isn't a way out either — the current simulator runtime refuses
to install x86_64 simulator apps ("Failed to find matching arch").

**Workaround**, in case it helps others: build the missing slice from source and merge it
into the template, then repack `ios.zip`:

    scons platform=ios target=template_debug arch=arm64 simulator=yes
    lipo -create <arm64-sim libgodot.a> <template x86_64 libgodot.a> -output libgodot.a

Note this is wiped by every editor/template update.

Since the metadata promises an architecture the binary doesn't contain, it may be worth
either shipping the arm64 slice or correcting the Info.plist so the failure surfaces
earlier with a clearer error.

OK, Since everyone seems to be stumbling with this, 
and nobody comes forward with a definitive solution, or door shut...

### ---- Custom iOS Templates with Simulator Support ---- (made by **Claude AI**)
(Working with Godot 4.6.2 Stable, probably with 4.6.3 too; 4.7+ will need confirmation..)

export SCRIPT_AES256_ENCRYPTION_KEY="YOUR_KEY"

mkdir -p "$HOME/Projects/Godot Source/4.6.3 Stable/godot_temp_libs_ios"


 PHASE 1: COMPILE STATIC LIBRARIES (.a files)
================================================================================
Navigate to your Godot Source directory and run the builds:

cd "$HOME/Projects/Godot Source/4.6.3 Stable/godot-4.6.3-stable"

```
# iOS Device Release
rm -rf bin/obj/ && rm -f bin/*.a && mkdir -p bin/obj
scons platform=ios arch=arm64 target=template_release module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra lto=full debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)
if [ ! -f bin/libgodot.ios.template_release.arm64.a ]; then scons platform=ios arch=arm64 target=template_release module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra lto=full debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu); fi
cp bin/libgodot.ios.template_release.arm64.a ../godot_temp_libs_ios/

# iOS Device Debug
rm -rf bin/obj/ && rm -f bin/*.a && mkdir -p bin/obj
scons platform=ios arch=arm64 target=template_debug module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)
if [ ! -f bin/libgodot.ios.template_debug.arm64.a ]; then scons platform=ios arch=arm64 target=template_debug module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu); fi
cp bin/libgodot.ios.template_debug.arm64.a ../godot_temp_libs_ios/

# iOS Simulator Release
rm -rf bin/obj/ && rm -f bin/*.a && mkdir -p bin/obj
scons platform=ios arch=arm64 ios_simulator=yes target=template_release module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra lto=full debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)
if [ ! -f bin/libgodot.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.a ]; then scons platform=ios arch=arm64 ios_simulator=yes target=template_release module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra lto=full debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu); fi
cp bin/libgodot.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.a ../godot_temp_libs_ios/

# iOS Simulator Debug
rm -rf bin/obj/ && rm -f bin/*.a && mkdir -p bin/obj
scons platform=ios arch=arm64 ios_simulator=yes target=template_debug module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)
if [ ! -f bin/libgodot.ios.template_debug.arm64.simulator.a ]; then scons platform=ios arch=arm64 ios_simulator=yes target=template_debug module_mono_enabled=no optimize=size_extra debug_symbols=no deprecated=yes profile=CUSTOM.PY build_feature_profile=4.6.3_iOS.gdbuild -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu); fi
cp bin/libgodot.ios.template_debug.arm64.simulator.a ../godot_temp_libs_ios/
```

(command is run twice to prevent compiled file from being auto Deleted...
It happens in linux, so I also double it in macOS..)

 PHASE 2: ASSEMBLING THE XCFRAMEWORK BUNDLES
================================================================================
Run from anywhere. This packages the raw .a files into Apple frameworks.

```
OUTPUT_DIR="$HOME/Projects/Godot Source/4.6.3 Stable/godot_ios_templates_output"
LIBS="$HOME/Projects/Godot Source/4.6.3 Stable/godot_temp_libs_ios"
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

echo "📦 Assembling Release XCFramework..."
XCF_REL="$OUTPUT_DIR/libgodot.ios.release.xcframework"
rm -rf "$XCF_REL" && mkdir -p "$XCF_REL/ios-arm64" "$XCF_REL/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"
cp "$LIBS/libgodot.ios.template_release.arm64.a" "$XCF_REL/ios-arm64/libgodot.a"
cp "$LIBS/libgodot.ios.template_release.arm64.simulator.a" "$XCF_REL/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libgodot.a"
touch "$XCF_REL/ios-arm64/empty" "$XCF_REL/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/empty"

cat > "$XCF_REL/Info.plist" << 'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>AvailableLibraries</key>
    <array>
        <dict>
            <key>LibraryIdentifier</key>
            <string>ios-arm64</string>
            <key>LibraryPath</key>
            <string>libgodot.a</string>
            <key>SupportedArchitectures</key>
            <array><string>arm64</string></array>
            <key>SupportedPlatform</key>
            <string>ios</string>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>LibraryIdentifier</key>
            <string>ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator</string>
            <key>LibraryPath</key>
            <string>libgodot.a</string>
            <key>SupportedArchitectures</key>
            <array><string>arm64</string><string>x86_64</string></array>
            <key>SupportedPlatform</key>
            <string>ios</string>
            <key>SupportedPlatformVariant</key>
            <string>simulator</string>
        </dict>
    </array>
    <key>CFBundlePackageType</key>
    <string>XFWK</string>
    <key>XCFrameworkFormatVersion</key>
    <string>1.0</string>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF

echo "📦 Assembling Debug XCFramework..."
XCF_DBG="$OUTPUT_DIR/libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework"
rm -rf "$XCF_DBG" && mkdir -p "$XCF_DBG/ios-arm64" "$XCF_DBG/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"
cp "$LIBS/libgodot.ios.template_debug.arm64.a" "$XCF_DBG/ios-arm64/libgodot.a"
cp "$LIBS/libgodot.ios.template_debug.arm64.simulator.a" "$XCF_DBG/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libgodot.a"
touch "$XCF_DBG/ios-arm64/empty" "$XCF_DBG/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/empty"
cp "$XCF_REL/Info.plist" "$XCF_DBG/Info.plist"
```

 PHASE 3: SPLICING THE STOCK IOS.ZIP (FIXED ZIP ROOT)
================================================================================
This extracts the stock Godot templates, replaces the unoptimized engine with
our custom built ones, and correctly repacks them at the ZIP root.

```
OUTPUT_DIR="$HOME/Projects/Godot Source/4.6.3 Stable/godot_ios_templates_output"
STOCK_IOS_ZIP="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.6.3.stable/ios.zip"
IOS_STAGING="$OUTPUT_DIR/ios_staging"

echo "🧹 Cleaning and Extracting stock ios.zip..."
rm -rf "$IOS_STAGING"
mkdir -p "$IOS_STAGING/temp_extract" "$IOS_STAGING/ios"
unzip -q "$STOCK_IOS_ZIP" -d "$IOS_STAGING/temp_extract"

if [ -d "$IOS_STAGING/temp_extract/ios" ]; then
    mv "$IOS_STAGING/temp_extract/ios/"* "$IOS_STAGING/ios/"
else
    mv "$IOS_STAGING/temp_extract/"* "$IOS_STAGING/ios/"
fi
rm -rf "$IOS_STAGING/temp_extract"

echo "🔄 Swapping in custom XCFrameworks..."
rm -rf "$IOS_STAGING/ios/libgodot.ios.release.xcframework"
rm -rf "$IOS_STAGING/ios/libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework"
cp -r "$OUTPUT_DIR/libgodot.ios.release.xcframework" "$IOS_STAGING/ios/"
cp -r "$OUTPUT_DIR/libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework" "$IOS_STAGING/ios/"
find "$IOS_STAGING" -name ".DS_Store" -delete

echo "🤐 Repacking custom ios.zip (files directly at root)..."
rm -f "$OUTPUT_DIR/ios.zip"
cd "$IOS_STAGING/ios" || exit
zip -r -9 "$OUTPUT_DIR/ios.zip" * > /dev/null
echo "✅ Phase 3 Complete! Zip ready."
```

 PHASE 4: INSTALLATION TO GODOT FOLDERS
================================================================================
Creates a safe "4.6.3.custom" folder in Godot's export_templates directory so
we don't overwrite the original official stable templates.

```
OUTPUT_DIR="$HOME/Projects/Godot Source/4.6.3 Stable/godot_ios_templates_output"
FINAL="$OUTPUT_DIR/CustomTemplates"
STOCK="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.6.3.stable"
DEST="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.6.3.custom"

echo "🏗️ Assembling the complete template set..."
rm -rf "$FINAL" && mkdir -p "$FINAL"
cp "$OUTPUT_DIR/ios.zip" "$FINAL/"

for f in "$STOCK"/*; do
    fname=$(basename "$f")
    if [ "$fname" != "ios.zip" ]; then
        cp -r "$f" "$FINAL/"
    fi
done

echo "4.6.3.custom" > "$FINAL/version.txt"

echo "🚀 Installing to Godot..."
rm -rf "$DEST" && mkdir -p "$DEST"
cp -r "$FINAL/"* "$DEST/"

echo "✅ DONE! In Godot iOS Export Preset, point the 'Custom Template' field to:"
echo "$DEST/ios.zip"
```

----------------------

-After finishing the process, simply Copy the new custom **ios.zip** file into the right folder,
 /Users/USERNAME/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.6.3.Stable/
